title: Vector Databases
subtitle: Embeddings, similarity search, and vector stores
author: KERNAL Team

whyItExists.problem: LLM embeddings are dense 768-3072 dimensional vectors. Traditional databases (SQL, key-value) cannot efficiently search millions of vectors for semantic nearest neighbors — a linear scan over 1M × 1536-dim vectors takes seconds.
whyItExists.solution: Vector databases use Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) algorithms (HNSW, IVF) to index and search high-dimensional vectors in milliseconds. They are purpose-built for the retrieval phase of RAG pipelines.
whyItExists.whenToUse: When you need semantic search over more than ~10K documents. For small collections, in-memory FAISS or ChromaDB works. For production scale (millions of vectors), use Pinecone, Weaviate, or pgvector.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: If you have fewer than 10K chunks, a simple in-memory list + numpy cosine similarity is fast enough and simpler. Don't add vector DB infrastructure for small use cases.

explainModes.beginner: A vector database is a special filing system for AI knowledge. Instead of searching by exact words, it searches by meaning — 'best Italian food' and 'finest pasta restaurant' are filed close together because they mean similar things.
explainModes.simple: Every piece of text is converted to a list of numbers (a vector) that captures its meaning. A vector database stores millions of these number lists and can quickly find the ones most similar to a query — even if they use different words.
explainModes.standard: Vector databases store embedding vectors alongside metadata. At query time, they perform ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search using algorithms like HNSW to find semantically similar vectors in O(log n) time. They return the original document chunks for use in RAG prompts.
explainModes.technical: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) builds a multi-layer graph where each node is an embedding vector. Search traverses from coarse to fine layers, following nearest-neighbor edges. IVF (Inverted File Index) clusters vectors into Voronoi cells and searches only the nearest cells. Both achieve <10ms retrieval at million-scale.
explainModes.deepDive: Production vector stores offer filtering (metadata filter + ANN combined), namespaces (per-tenant isolation), and hybrid search (combine dense + sparse BM25 scores). pgvector brings vector search to PostgreSQL: CREATE EXTENSION vector; allows VECTOR columns and <-> (L2), <=> (cosine), <#> (inner product) operators with ivfflat or hnsw index types.

content.text: Vector databases store embedding vectors and perform approximate nearest-neighbour (ANN) search to find semantically similar content in milliseconds. They are the retrieval backbone of every production RAG system.

content.definition: A list of floats (e.g., 1536 dimensions for text-embedding-3-small) representing the semantic meaning of text. Similar texts have geometrically close vectors. Distance metrics: cosine similarity, dot product, Euclidean distance.
A distance metric: cos(θ) = (A·B)/(|A||B|). Ranges from -1 (opposite) to 1 (identical). Used because it measures angle, not magnitude — so text length doesn't bias similarity scores.

content.code:
# pip install chromadb
import chromadb

client = chromadb.Client()  # In-memory (dev/prototype)
# For persistence: chromadb.PersistentClient(path="./chroma_db")

collection = client.create_collection(
    name="docs",
    metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"}  # cosine similarity
)

# Add documents (ChromaDB auto-embeds with default model)
collection.add(
    documents=[
        "Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for caching and pub/sub",
        "MongoDB is a NoSQL document database storing JSON-like BSON documents",
        "PostgreSQL is a relational database with ACID compliance and SQL support",
        "Pinecone is a managed vector database optimised for semantic search at scale",
    ],
    ids=["doc1", "doc2", "doc3", "doc4"]
)

# Semantic search
results = collection.query(
    query_texts=["What database should I use for caching?"],
    n_results=2
)
print(results["documents"])  # ['Redis is an in-memory...', ...]  — correct!
print(results["distances"])  # Cosine distances

a.name: ChromaDB
a.description: Open-source, runs locally or self-hosted. Great for prototyping and small-medium scale.
a.useWhen: Prototyping, side projects, internal tools with <1M vectors

b.name: Pinecone
b.description: Fully managed cloud vector database. Scales to billions of vectors.
b.useWhen: Production apps, multi-tenant SaaS, >1M vectors, need 99.9% uptime SLA

content.code:
# pip install pinecone-client openai
from pinecone import Pinecone
from openai import OpenAI

pc = Pinecone(api_key="YOUR_PINECONE_KEY")
oai = OpenAI()

# Create or connect to an index
index = pc.Index("docs-index")

def embed(text: str) -> list[float]:
    return oai.embeddings.create(
        input=text, model="text-embedding-3-small"
    ).data[0].embedding

# Upsert vectors with metadata
vectors = [
    {"id": "chunk_1", "values": embed("Redis caching guide"), "metadata": {"source": "redis_docs.pdf", "page": 1}},
    {"id": "chunk_2", "values": embed("MongoDB aggregation pipeline"), "metadata": {"source": "mongo_docs.pdf", "page": 5}},
]
index.upsert(vectors=vectors)

# Query with metadata filter
results = index.query(
    vector=embed("How do I cache API responses?"),
    top_k=3,
    filter={"source": {"$eq": "redis_docs.pdf"}},  # only search Redis docs
    include_metadata=True
)
for match in results.matches:
    print(f"Score: {match.score:.3f} | Source: {match.metadata['source']}")

# pip install psycopg2-binary pgvector
import psycopg2
from pgvector.psycopg2 import register_vector
from openai import OpenAI

oai = OpenAI()

# Connect and enable extension
conn = psycopg2.connect("postgresql://user:pass@localhost/mydb")
register_vector(conn)
cur = conn.cursor()

# Create table with vector column
cur.execute("""
    CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS docs (
        id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
        content TEXT,
        embedding VECTOR(1536),
        source VARCHAR
    );
    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS docs_embedding_idx ON docs
        USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);
""")
conn.commit()

# Insert a document
content = "Redis is used for session storage and caching"
embedding = oai.embeddings.create(input=content, model="text-embedding-3-small").data[0].embedding
cur.execute("INSERT INTO docs (content, embedding, source) VALUES (%s, %s, %s)",
            (content, embedding, "redis_guide.pdf"))
conn.commit()

# Cosine similarity search
query_emb = oai.embeddings.create(input="How to cache data?", model="text-embedding-3-small").data[0].embedding
cur.execute("""
    SELECT content, 1 - (embedding <=> %s::vector) AS similarity
    FROM docs ORDER BY similarity DESC LIMIT 3""", (query_emb,))
for row in cur.fetchall():
    print(f"Similarity: {row[1]:.3f} | {row[0][:60]}")

content.text: For production, use managed vector DBs like Pinecone, Weaviate, or pgvector (Postgres extension). ChromaDB is excellent for prototyping but requires self-managed scaling.

questions.question: What does a vector database use to find similar documents?
options: SQL LIKE queries on text columns
questions.explanation: Vector databases compute cosine similarity (or dot product, or L2 distance) between query and document embeddings to find semantic matches — not exact word matches.

questions.question: Why is ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) used instead of exact nearest neighbor?
options: Exact search is O(n) over all vectors — too slow for millions of vectors. ANN is O(log n) with minimal accuracy loss
Exact search doesn't work in high dimensions
questions.explanation: Exact nearest neighbor requires comparing the query to all n vectors — O(n). For 10M vectors at 1536 dims, this takes seconds. HNSW and IVF index the space to find approximate nearest neighbors in <10ms.

questions.question: What advantage does pgvector offer over dedicated vector databases?
options: It is faster for billion-scale search
It runs vector search inside PostgreSQL, letting you combine metadata filtering with SQL queries in one database
It supports all embedding models natively
questions.explanation: pgvector adds vector columns and ANN indexes to PostgreSQL. This lets you combine semantic search with relational queries (JOINs, WHERE clauses) without maintaining a separate database.

faq.q: What embedding model should I use?
faq.a: For English-only: text-embedding-3-small (OpenAI, 1536 dims, cheap and fast). For multilingual: multilingual-e5-large or Cohere embed-multilingual-v3. Always use the SAME model for indexing and querying.

faq.q: How many vectors can ChromaDB handle?
faq.a: ChromaDB works well up to ~1M vectors on a single machine. Beyond that, use a managed solution (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant) or pgvector with dedicated storage.

Most vector databases allow filtering by document metadata before or alongside vector search. Example: search only documents from 2024 or only from department='engineering'. This prevents irrelevant results from other data segments.

usedIn: Duplicate detection in large document corpora

Code search tools that find semantically similar functions
